title: Understanding the CI/CD Workflow Lifecycle knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Understanding the CI/CD Workflow Lifecycle?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
A workflow run moves from a triggering event through scheduling and runner execution to logs, status checks, outputs, artifacts, and optional deployment.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: A workflow run moves from a triggering event through scheduling and runner execution to logs, status checks, outputs, artifacts, and optional deployment.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of understanding the ci/cd workflow lifecycle: A workflow run moves from a triggering event through scheduling and runner execution to logs, status checks, outputs, artifacts, and optional deployment. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Source-code changes”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: For source-code changes, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: For source-code changes, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.
questions.explanation: Source-code changes: For source-code changes, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to understanding the ci/cd workflow lifecycle?
options: Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: A workflow run moves from a triggering event through scheduling and runner execution to logs, status checks, outputs, artifacts, and optional deployment. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
